Ikon is an internationally acclaimed contemporary art venue located in Birmingham, UK. Free entry.

[DONATE](https://www.ikon-gallery.org/make-a-donation)

## IKON SHOP

Browse books, prints, stationery, jewellery, homeware and gifts.

All profits support Ikon’s charitable artistic and educational programme.

[SHOP ONLINE](https://shop.ikon-gallery.org/)

## HIRE IKON FOR YOUR EVENT

Housed in a beautiful Victorian building, Ikon Gallery has versatile spaces, accommodating 10 to 500 guests.

Get in touch today to discuss your event with a member of our team.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://www.ikon-gallery.org/about/venue-hire)

## ART IN PRISONS

Ikon’s _Art in Prisons_ programme places artist residencies in three prisons: HMP Grendon and HMP Spring Hill in Buckinghamshire, and HMP Birmingham. Each residency shares the core belief that art practice can be a force for good in carceral settings.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://www.ikon-gallery.org/off-site/art-in-prisons)

## CREATIVE HEALTH

Ikon Creative Health explores the dynamic intersections of art, health and wellbeing. Through research, exhibitions and workshops, Ikon works with artists, academics, communities and healthcare partners to explore how art can support health.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://www.ikon-gallery.org/creative-health)

## IKON YOUTH PROGRAMME

Ikon Youth Programme (IYP) navigates the waterways on board [_Slow Boat_,](https://www.ikon-gallery.org/education/ikon-youth-programme/history-of-slow-boat/) a converted narrow boat. IYP are collaborating with creative thinkers and makers to reimagine _Slow Boat_ as a local art school.

Funded by Freelands Foundation.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://www.ikon-gallery.org/learning/ikon-youth-programme)

## ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY

Ikon is dedicated to minimising its impact on the environment and we strive to make our operations and exhibitions as sustainable as possible.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://www.ikon-gallery.org/about/environmental-sustainability)

Be inspired, 
by the sea.

[Plan your visit](https://turnercontemporary.org/visit-us)

Turner Contemporary is a contemporary art gallery located on Margate’s seafront, where the extraordinary light inspired JMW Turner. We present world-class exhibitions, creative workshops, learning programmes and community events. Entry is free.

[Read our story](https://turnercontemporary.org/our-story)

---

- [Exhibition](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibition) [**Sophie Calle: ** Something Missing?](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/sophie-calle-something-missing)

 Sat 3 Oct 2026–Sun 24 Jan 2027

 Free entry, give what you can

 This autumn, Turner Contemporary presents 'Sophie Calle: Something Missing?', the artist’s first institutional exhibition in Britain in over fifteen years.

 [Visit exhibition](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/sophie-calle-something-missing)

- [Nicole Eisenman: Perpetual Motion Machine with Museum Piece con Gas](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/nicole-eisenman-perpetual-motion-machine-with-museum-piece-con-gas 'Nicole Eisenman: Perpetual Motion Machine with Museum Piece con Gas')

 [Display](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/display) [**Nicole Eisenman: Perpetual Motion Machine with Museum Piece con Gas**](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/nicole-eisenman-perpetual-motion-machine-with-museum-piece-con-gas)

 14 November 2026–11 April 2027

 Free entry, give what you can

 Nicole Eisenman draws on the language of figurative art and her deep knowledge of art history to create incisive, often humorous, observations on contemporary life. 

 [View display](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/nicole-eisenman-perpetual-motion-machine-with-museum-piece-con-gas)

- [JMW Turner: Breaking Waves](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/turner-250-breaking-waves 'JMW Turner: Breaking Waves')

 [Display](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/display) [**JMW Turner: Breaking Waves**](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/turner-250-breaking-waves)

 Apr 2025–2027

 Free entry, give what you can

 Join us to see JMW Turner’s oil sketch 'Waves Breaking on a Lee Shore at Margate (Study for ‘Rockets and Blue Lights’)' at Turner, part of a year-long festival celebrating 250 years since the artist's birth.

 [Visit display](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/turner-250-breaking-waves)

- [The Drawing Studio](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/the-drawing-studio 'The Drawing Studio')

 [Clore Learning Studio](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/clore-learning-studio) [**The Drawing Studio**](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/the-drawing-studio)

 Sat 22 Nov 2025–2027

 Free entry, give what you can

 We’ve transformed our Clore Learning Studio into a cabinet of curiosities full of inspiration and surprises to make drawing fun.

 [Visit studio](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/the-drawing-studio)

- [I Never Stopped Loving You](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/i-never-stopped-loving-you 'I Never Stopped Loving You')

 [Display](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/display) [**I Never Stopped Loving You**](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/i-never-stopped-loving-you)

 Since 2010

 Outdoor artwork

 Tracey Emin's love letter to her hometown lights up Droit House on the Harbour arm. I Never Stopped Loving You uses Emin's own handwriting moulded in pink neon to reflect her feelings across the main sands to Margate.

 [Visit artwork](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/i-never-stopped-loving-you)

- [Antony Gormley: Another Time](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/another-time 'Antony Gormley: Another Time')

 [Commission](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/commission) [**Antony Gormley: Another Time**](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/another-time)

 Since 2017

 Outdoor commission

 See one of a series of one hundred, solid cast-iron figures by Antony Gormley exploring the experience of being human.

 [Visit commission](https://turnercontemporary.org/whats-on/exhibitions/another-time)

## Upcoming exhibitions

The first exhibition of the work of Fiona Lutjenhuis in the UK explores alternative belief systems, moral judgement - taking you into the realms of Hell and Atlantis

[**Dana Awartani**](https://www.trg.ed.ac.uk/exhibition/dana-awartani)

## 29 Jun – 26 Sep 2027

In summer 2027, Talbot Rice Gallery will present a major solo exhibition by Saudi Arabian-Palestinian artist Dana Awartani. 

[**The Isles of Many Gods**](https://www.trg.ed.ac.uk/exhibition/isles-many-gods)

## 23 Oct 2027 – 12 Feb 2028

_The Isles of Many Gods_ is a major group exhibition made in response to the rise of anti-migrant hostility and racialised violence. Focused on artists based in the UK, the exhibition proposes art and collective imagination as forces for consciousness-raising, solidarity and social change.

### Plan your visit

The Hayward Gallery is also where you’ll find the HENI Project Space.

##### Getting here

Our address is Southbank Centre, Belvedere Road, London, SE1 8XX.

The nearest tube stations to us are Waterloo and Embankment; Waterloo is also the nearest train station. And more than 20 different London bus routes pass within 500 metres of our venues.  More information on getting here by rail, road or river is available on [our Getting here page](https://www.southbankcentre.co.uk/visit-us/getting-here/).

##### Cloakroom

We have a cloakroom for coats, umbrellas and small bags; it costs £2 per item.

##### We’re cash-free

Please note that we’re unable to accept cash payments across our venues.

### Access

We’re working hard to remove barriers, so that our facilities and events can be accessible to as many people as possible.

All help points, toilets, performance and exhibition spaces at the Southbank Centre are accessible to all, as are the cafes, bars and restaurants. We also have excellent public transport links with step-free access.

All information about booking wheelchair spaces, step-free access, blue badge parking, access maps and guides and other help available whilst you’re here, including details about our Access Scheme, can be found on [our Access page](https://www.southbankcentre.co.uk/visit-us/access/).

### Exhibition tours

Guided tours of our Hayward Gallery exhibitions are available to ticket holders; the dates and times of these can be found when you click through to book your exhibition tickets.

If you’d like to arrange a private/group tour of an exhibition, [please contact us](https://www.southbankcentre.co.uk/contact-us/). The Hayward Gallery does not accept external tour guides or tour groups – all exhibition tours must be arranged through the Southbank Centre.

### Food & drink

Offering sandwiches, salads, cakes and coffee, [Hayward Gallery Cafe](https://www.southbankcentre.co.uk/food-and-drink/hayward-gallery-cafe/) is the perfect spot for a pre-exhibition energy boost or a post-visit drink.

From coffee to cocktails, filling favourites to fine dining, plus some of London’s best street food – it’s all here at the Southbank Centre.

[Other places to eat and drink whilst you’re here](https://www.southbankcentre.co.uk/food-and-drink/)
